projects.name: ImHere
refine: Error association and focus recovery — implemented
expand: Validate one ambiguous attendance scenario with students and instructors
Document actual capstone contribution and policy constraints
remove: Any implication that a failed permission proves absence
Claims of authentication or a persistent audit service
signatures: A correction before commitment
A record with its reason attached
Different density for different responsibilities
projects.test: Ask a student to explain a failed check-in, then ask an instructor to resolve it. Observe whether either confuses a closed session with an absence.
projects.tradeoff: The extra correction step slows faculty entry but makes a consequential decision inspectable.

audit.Purpose: Explain a consequential shared record across student and faculty responsibilities.
audit.Role value: Primary: UX, product and interaction design. Secondary: UI and design technology.
audit.First impression: The navy record composition shows a disputed state rather than a decorative dashboard. Keep this as the default opener.
audit.Concept: Strong because uncertainty has a human consequence: a missed check-in must not become an unexplained absence.
audit.UX: Current/proposed values, required rationale, cancel, review requests and record history demonstrate substantive decision logic.
audit.UI: Dense faculty rows contrast with a focused student workspace. This is a useful example of density changing by role.
audit.Graphic design: The context-first poster and check-in guide support the product. They are supporting applications, not a full institutional brand commission.
audit.Visual identity: Navy rules, orange exceptions and numbered records belong to an academic service. The compact ih mark is a functional typographic signature.
audit.Typography: Plus Jakarta Sans handles the interface; IBM Plex Mono identifies records. Navigation was raised to 14 px in this pass.
audit.Colour: Ink #142B49, blue #164B8D and orange #EC9A51. Exception colour always needs a written state.
audit.Art direction: The record itself is the hero. Avoid stock campus photos, biometric imagery or fake location maps.
audit.Systems thinking: Role views share sample state while session status, attendance and review requests remain different concepts.
audit.Accessibility: The correction field now exposes aria-invalid and its error description. Manual keyboard and screen-reader review are still required.
audit.Responsiveness: Student and faculty layouts adapt differently. Source breakpoints exist; no real-device conformance is claimed.
audit.Interaction: Submit a correction, inspect its prior state and return to the student view. Form errors focus the relevant field.
audit.Case study: The new scan strip makes origin, work shown and the best interaction visible. Replace generic section headings with the record’s actual stakes.
audit.Differentiation: The most institutional and consequential project in the collection. Keep it visually distant from AFTERFORM and the editorial products.
audit.Believability: Credible as a prototype. There is no authentication, campus integration, location collection or durable audit storage.
audit.Hiring value: Explaining a state transition, protecting a draft and distinguishing interface roles from backend permissions.
audit.Main weakness: Institutional policies, original role attribution and raw research evidence remain unverified. A persuasive flow does not establish fairness in practice.

projects.name: AFTERFORM
keep: Recent identity and all original artwork
refine: Fast project facts and direct proposal link — implemented
Default homepage position after ImHere — implemented
expand: Print at actual size and make an envelope dummy
Review proposal wording with repairers and people bringing garments
remove: Further decorative collateral without a service role
Any implication that a dimensional prototype is a production-approved die
signatures: Object → attention → next action
A label that knows the next step
Approval belongs to a revision
The same request on screen and paper
projects.test: Ask someone to distinguish their preference from the studio’s proposal, then change the scope and ask whether the earlier approval still applies.
projects.tradeoff: The identity is expressive at invitation scale and restrained where someone must understand scope, price or permission.

audit.Purpose: Show how a repair service’s identity can carry useful information across screen, paper and garment.
audit.Role value: Primary: graphic, visual and brand design. Strong supporting product/UI and editorial evidence.
audit.First impression: The existing brand-system board and large wordmark establish a complete identity immediately. Preserve the recent refinement.
audit.Concept: Repair is a considered change, not a purchase funnel. That premise gives the brand and approval model a shared purpose.
audit.UX: A request is distinct from a proposal; a question keeps approval pending; revised scope invalidates the old approval.
audit.UI: The plum repair desk has meaningful form states, scope review, revision context and a paper brief derived from saved data.
audit.Graphic design: The 24-page publication, 16-page standards, labels, service forms, campaign and environmental studies are the richest graphic evidence in the portfolio.
audit.Visual identity: Responsive service lockups, compact signature and joining mark form a usable family. Existing Bodoni letterforms are not claimed as a custom typeface.
audit.Typography: Bodoni Moda creates fashion character; Karla carries instructions; Inconsolata organises identifiers. Print and interface type have different jobs.
audit.Colour: Plum #38233F, vermilion #BD3B2F, lilac #D6C6EC and poplin #FAF7F8. The palette is retained, not recoloured for novelty.
audit.Art direction: Material close-ups and the physical kit support the garment concept. Generated application imagery remains labelled as illustration.
audit.Systems thinking: Object → attention → next action connects label zones, paper hierarchy and product decisions.
audit.Accessibility: Existing contrast calculations, persistent labels, reduced motion and publication text alternatives are inspectable. They are not a WCAG certificate.
audit.Responsiveness: The actual product and standards have narrow-screen rules; the case study needs device checks for the long brand word and dense specimens.
audit.Interaction: Question, approve, undo, revise, print and return from a sample record. Nine isolated studies make this depth easy to inspect.
audit.Case study: Keep the ecosystem pacing and flat artwork. Add only the concise project facts and direct decision link in this pass.
audit.Differentiation: A tactile repair-studio world, distinct from INTERVAL’s spatial programme and Áurea’s archive.
audit.Believability: Strong concept coherence. No operating repair studio, manufactured kit, real booking or customer outcome is claimed.
audit.Hiring value: A flexible identity with editorial depth and a functioning service model, not just a logo placed on objects.
audit.Main weakness: The next evidence is physical proofing and user/repairer validation. Another poster or rendered kit will not resolve that gap.

projects.name: Holland Walking Tour
refine: Paper companion uses the chosen order — implemented
expand: Verify a real short route with local sources
Observe older visitors using pause and text size outdoors
remove: Any suggested walking time treated as measured fact
signatures: Your pace as an interaction rule
One current story outdoors
The same chosen sequence on paper
projects.test: Ask an older visitor to choose two stories, explain what they selected, pause, return and enlarge the text outside.
projects.tradeoff: Manual progression gives predictable control but cannot substitute for location-aware navigation.

audit.Purpose: Make a self-guided visitor experience readable, predictable and comfortable for older adults.
audit.Role value: Primary: UX, web and accessible interaction design. Supporting information and civic graphic design.
audit.First impression: Real Holland photography and teal wayfinding distinguish the place before the interface is explained.
audit.Concept: The visitor’s pace is a useful organizing idea. It must not imply verified distances or access conditions that the prototype does not contain.
audit.UX: Chosen stories appear before a deliberate Start action. Pause, resume and previous preserve orientation.
audit.UI: Three main visitor destinations and a separate content studio reduce role confusion. Large text is a genuine control.
audit.Graphic design: The poster now connects to a printable chosen-story companion. This adds a useful physical application rather than a decorative map.
audit.Visual identity: Heritage-influenced display type, teal, yellow markers and numbered observations create a welcoming civic identity.
audit.Typography: DM Serif Display welcomes; Source Sans 3 carries reading and controls. Existing 18 px body and 22 px option are retained.
audit.Colour: Ink #233F42, teal #176369, pale background #F6F9F8 and yellow #EED785. Yellow marks a stage; text remains dark.
audit.Art direction: Keep credited documentary streetscapes. Do not substitute imaginary Dutch scenery or fabricated historical photographs.
audit.Systems thinking: Story records are reusable; editorial readiness requires explicit source, image and route checks.
audit.Accessibility: Large controls, reading preference, quiet mode and written progress are meaningful provisions. Outdoor glare and older-user testing remain open.
audit.Responsiveness: The active experience prioritizes the current story on mobile rather than shrinking the route summary.
audit.Interaction: A chosen sequence carries into the new paper view. Leaving the preview and returning does not change the selection.
audit.Case study: New headings foreground reassurance rather than generic UX process. The original collaboration context remains qualified.
audit.Differentiation: A civic place-led experience with larger text and calmer interaction. It should not become another luxury editorial archive.
audit.Believability: The current content is observation prompts, not a verified tour. Its usefulness as an actual walking service requires local route work.
audit.Hiring value: Prioritizing cognitive simplicity, readable information and a visitor’s control over pace.
audit.Main weakness: Verified route content, accessibility conditions and original research documentation are missing. A more polished mockup cannot supply them.

projects.name: INTERVAL
refine: Immediate evidence link and project context — implemented
Place within role-specific homepage paths — implemented
expand: Run one plan-building task with conflicting preferences
Make a print dummy and test room recognition at distance
remove: Unverified floor plans or walking-time estimates
Any checkout added only to increase screen count
signatures: The interval as space and time
One room number across channels
A plan that protects a break
projects.test: Give someone a short visit window and two overlapping interests. Ask them to build a plan and explain the effect of replacing a session.
projects.tradeoff: Excluding partial attendance makes filtering predictable but depends on a future real re-entry policy.

audit.Purpose: Connect an expressive listening-festival identity with a realistic personal programme and room system.
audit.Role value: Primary: product, visual, graphic and information design. Strong supporting editorial and interaction evidence.
audit.First impression: Wide Unbounded type, acid lime and a deliberate gap make a recognisable cultural identity.
audit.Concept: An interval works both as graphic space and time between sessions. This is the clearest identity-to-function connection after AFTERFORM.
audit.UX: Arrival/departure constraints, conflicts, preferred gaps and explicit replacement demonstrate prioritization and alternate paths.
audit.UI: Timetable rows support comparison; session conditions remain visible; personal planning does not pretend to be ticketing.
audit.Graphic design: Six distinct posters, a 12-page guide, signs, listening card, email and social formats show controlled variation.
audit.Visual identity: The split name, room numbers and repeated intervals create recognition without relying on a logo on every item.
audit.Typography: Unbounded for voice; Instrument Sans for conditions; monospace times for scanability. Do not use wide display type for dense instructions.
audit.Colour: Ink #191B18, paper #F3F2EC, lime #D9F44C and surface #FFFEF8. Lime is a recognition cue, not a colour-only availability signal.
audit.Art direction: Listening room, magnetic tape and strings are relevant material imagery. The application images are illustrative, not festival documentation.
audit.Systems thinking: Room 01/02/03 connects programme, guide, sign and room details. Editing a plan invalidates a stale sample pass.
audit.Accessibility: Visible conditions, reversible choices and text/print exports help comprehension. Venue accessibility and assistive-technology use are not proven.
audit.Responsiveness: Time, title and conditions reorganize from desktop rows into mobile reading blocks. Three screen-study widths expose intended behavior.
audit.Interaction: Conflict replacement, gap alternatives, Undo, interest saving and portable plan demonstrate more than an ideal booking path.
audit.Case study: Retain the varied editorial case study. The new scan strip sends product reviewers straight to a short-break plan.
audit.Differentiation: A cultural, spatial, typographic world; not a generic event ticket app or a second garment brand.
audit.Believability: Eight sessions and three rooms are authored samples. No venue booking, real capacity, waitlist submission or visitor count exists.
audit.Hiring value: Making identity, content architecture and product decisions reinforce one another.
audit.Main weakness: The real festival policies and physical wayfinding need testing. The selected visual references are not audience research.

projects.name: Áurea
refine: Journal error semantics and persistent result feedback — implemented
expand: Test plain-language versus expert note vocabulary
Use a larger, properly sourced dataset before claiming scale
remove: Claims that notes identify allergens or predict wear
signatures: A note as an entry point
Replace one comparison rather than reset both
A printable record that leaves room for uncertainty
projects.test: Ask a beginner to find a note they recognise, compare two profiles and recover from an over-specific query. Ask them to explain what the sheet does not tell them.
projects.tradeoff: Two records limit breadth but preserve side-by-side readability and a manageable replacement decision.

audit.Purpose: Make perfume information discoverable through taxonomy, comparable profiles and personal observations.
audit.Role value: Primary: UI, information and web design. Secondary: visual identity and interaction design.
audit.First impression: The oxblood editorial archive and note hierarchy communicate perfume without a decorative luxury checkout.
audit.Concept: A perfume database is a better premise than an invented perfume shop. Preserve search and records as the main task.
audit.UX: Search, family and notes support different vocabulary. Independent filter removal and a two-record replacement choice preserve intent.
audit.UI: A list/grid index, note directory, dossier and aligned comparison create a coherent information product.
audit.Graphic design: The new sampling sheet turns selected records into printable note columns and personal observation space. It uses the archive’s actual hierarchy.
audit.Visual identity: Italiana, oxblood rules, warm paper and a citron code distinguish the archive from Novella’s reading journal.
audit.Typography: Italiana only at display scale; DM Sans for search, tags and structured records. No thin serif metadata.
audit.Colour: Ink #302529, oxblood #713C46, paper #FCFAF5 and citron #E7D875. Citron supports indexing; it is not a health classification.
audit.Art direction: Perfume still lifes are clearly illustrative. Keep exact taxonomy in HTML rather than inside generated bottle labels.
audit.Systems thinking: One record model supplies cards, detail, comparison and print. UI components use the same family/note distinctions.
audit.Accessibility: Filter status, comparison headers and form labels already exist. This pass associates journal errors and restores focus after removed actions.
audit.Responsiveness: Comparison stays a labelled two-record region; the print preview becomes one column on narrow screens and two columns on paper.
audit.Interaction: Selection replacement, removable filters, no-results recovery and a saved-impression form are inspectable. Search feedback now uses a persistent status region.
audit.Case study: Specific headings now describe the vocabulary and decision problem. The paper connection makes the graphic work useful.
audit.Differentiation: Premium reference typography plus database structure, not a bookstore or a general lifestyle brand.
audit.Believability: Three original sample records are honest but too small to prove catalogue-scale findability or expert taxonomy.
audit.Hiring value: Balancing atmosphere with structured information and explaining what a classification can and cannot mean.
audit.Main weakness: No real catalogue or fragrance-community vocabulary study. The next step is a taxonomy task with representative records, not more fictional bottle brands.

projects.name: Loopline
refine: Field-linked errors and 14 px navigation — implemented
expand: Interview kitchen and receiving-partner stakeholders with permission
Verify who owns eligibility, timing changes and failed handoffs
remove: Any apparent food-safety certification or live driver tracking
signatures: A docket as a brand object
Eligibility before logistics
A preferred window without false confirmation
projects.test: Ask a partner who is unsure about eligibility to start a handoff, then ask who is responsible for clearing it and whether a pickup has been arranged.
projects.tradeoff: Pausing an uncertain handoff adds friction but prevents the interface from implying authority it does not have.

audit.Purpose: Make a food-rescue handoff understandable across kitchen and receiving-partner responsibilities.
audit.Role value: Primary: brand, communication and service-oriented UX. Supporting product and web design.
audit.First impression: Condensed GOOD FOOD. FURTHER. typography and a handoff docket give the identity energy and a practical reason to exist.
audit.Concept: The useful problem is coordinated information, not an unverified impact dashboard.
audit.UX: Eligibility precedes quantity and timing. Draft editing preserves the prior record until save, and cancellation restores it.
audit.UI: Four focused stages are clearer than a general logistics dashboard. Preferred timing is visibly distinct from an arranged pickup.
audit.Graphic design: The partner brief and handoff sheet are credible practical communication. Further merchandise would dilute the service.
audit.Visual identity: Forest, coral, yellow, square edges and dispatch-style labels differ from Nutriva’s rounded household notebook.
audit.Typography: Barlow Condensed gives public messages impact; Space Grotesk supports forms; IBM Plex Mono carries docket metadata.
audit.Colour: Forest #173629, coral #F15B40, yellow #F4C95D and paper #F4F0E8. Avoid using bright coral for small body copy.
audit.Art direction: Typography and clear field information should lead. Do not imply real recipients or show fabricated charitable impact photography.
audit.Systems thinking: Eligibility, record revision and preferred timing have explicit meanings. It is a handoff model, not a dispatch platform.
audit.Accessibility: Labels and errors now connect programmatically. The eligibility choice starts unselected; a new request cannot inherit a yes by default.
audit.Responsiveness: Forms are readable in one column on mobile; review information remains grouped by responsibility.
audit.Interaction: Explicit attestation, validation, cancel and revise demonstrate care around operational ambiguity.
audit.Case study: The new headings explain responsibility, and the scan link opens a fresh handoff rather than a decorative hero.
audit.Differentiation: Public-service energy expressed through condensed type and practical document structure.
audit.Believability: No donation clearance, driver availability, food-safety verification or actual pickup is provided. The original archive is marked as superseded.
audit.Hiring value: Recognising where software must defer to a real-world owner of a decision.
audit.Main weakness: Partner criteria, receiving capacity and operational policies are assumptions. The neutral eligibility default is a fix, not validation of the service.

projects.name: Novella
refine: Shelf focus recovery and larger navigation — implemented
expand: Test whether blind discovery adds value for different reading habits
Review long prose at zoom and in night mode
remove: Streaks, invented ratings and social mechanics without a reader need
signatures: A voice before a cover
The source stays with the passage
Typography as the product
projects.test: Ask a reader to try blind discovery, place a title on a shelf, keep a passage and explain where it came from later.
projects.tradeoff: A quiet experience gives up social proof and gamification in exchange for control; its value still needs reader evidence.

audit.Purpose: Create an editorial reading experience where readers control discovery and retain the context of saved words.
audit.Role value: Primary: web, UI and interaction design. Supporting editorial and visual design.
audit.First impression: The typographic excerpt establishes a quiet literary journal rather than another cover-card marketplace.
audit.Concept: Optional blind discovery offers a specific alternative to ratings-led choice. It should remain an option, not a gate.
audit.UX: Reveal, shelf placement and source-linked passages connect discovery to a personal collection.
audit.UI: Adjustable reading size, themes and a prose-first view demonstrate interface craft beyond a home screen.
audit.Graphic design: The new reading keepsake turns actual saved passages into a flat editorial composition with titles and room for annotation.
audit.Visual identity: Newsreader display, Libre Baskerville prose, Inter controls and cobalt details distinguish it from Áurea’s archival indexing.
audit.Typography: Prose uses generous line spacing and restrained measure. The print view shows typographic hierarchy without a device frame.
audit.Colour: Ink #272525, burgundy #6F3338 and paper #FAF9F6, with restrained blue in the graphic system. Night-reader contrast remains a separate check.
audit.Art direction: Original text carries the identity. Avoid invented literary reviews, real-author endorsements or unrelated book-cover art.
audit.Systems thinking: Shelf states are explicit. A passage keeps its source and supports undo; the print view uses the same saved set.
audit.Accessibility: Real text, adjustable type and visible controls are strengths. Shelf changes and removed passages now retain a useful keyboard focus target.
audit.Responsiveness: Reading measure and controls respond to screen width. The paper composition preserves reading hierarchy rather than printing navigation.
audit.Interaction: Blind reveal, passage deduplication, direct shelf placement and recovery provide a coherent loop.
audit.Case study: The story now foregrounds reader control and the source relationship. Keep it shorter than the product flagships.
audit.Differentiation: Literary and content-led, not the fragrance archive’s classification-led elegance.
audit.Believability: Three authored fiction samples are sufficient to demonstrate the interaction, not evidence of an operational reading platform.
audit.Hiring value: Designing with text as the main material, and carrying content meaning across formats.
audit.Main weakness: There is no reader study or licensed catalogue. This is supporting editorial/web evidence, not proof of a recommendation engine.

projects.name: Nutriva
refine: Focus recovery and intrinsic image sizes — implemented
expand: Study duplicate names, units and stale inventory in a real household task
Add quantities only after defining the model and authoritative recipe content
remove: Claims about reduced waste, grocery savings or verified meals
signatures: Why this ingredient is on the list
Correct the pantry, correct the plan
An off-screen list with its reasoning intact
projects.test: Give a household planner an outdated pantry, ask them to correct it, plan a meal and explain each missing item. Observe where name matching breaks.
projects.tradeoff: Ingredient-name matching is explainable and small enough to inspect; it cannot answer quantity or freshness questions.

audit.Purpose: Show understandable dependencies between pantry information, dinner choices and a shopping list.
audit.Role value: Primary: supporting product, UI and information design. Not the strongest opening project for graphic or brand roles.
audit.First impression: The kitchen checklist is friendly and legible, but the meal-planning category is less distinctive than the other concepts.
audit.Concept: Keep the narrow value: correcting inputs changes useful outputs. Avoid expanding into an unsupported nutrition or AI-coaching product.
audit.UX: Ingredient provenance and reversible pantry changes give it a meaningful systems story.
audit.UI: Ranked pantry fit, visible missing ingredients and a flexible plan are more credible than a mysterious recommendation score.
audit.Graphic design: The new shopping worksheet preserves meal provenance and checked status. This is a practical graphic application worth keeping.
audit.Visual identity: Rounded controls, DM Sans/Nunito, leaf green and butter yellow create a household tone. It needs no extra packaging or logo family.
audit.Typography: Readable 16–18 px interface copy and ingredient labels are the priority. Friendly display type should not obscure list scanning.
audit.Colour: Ink #203E2B, green #294B31, paper #F7F9F3 and yellow #F5DB54. Green is identity, not a nutrition claim.
audit.Art direction: Use the existing sample-meal photography with honest labels. Do not let polished food photos imply complete verified recipes.
audit.Systems thinking: Pantry, meal selection and derived grocery provenance share one small data model.
audit.Accessibility: Native checkbox labels and written provenance work without colour. Undo now receives focus when the removed control disappears.
audit.Responsiveness: The kitchen workspace stacks into a task-focused mobile flow. Print removes the navigation and keeps actionable list content.
audit.Interaction: Remove an ingredient, inspect changed matches, Undo, plan meals and see why an item appears on the list.
audit.Case study: The new headings make dependency reasoning explicit. Position last by default and earlier only in the UX/product path.
audit.Differentiation: Everyday consumer utility, deliberately less editorial and less institutional than the flagships.
audit.Believability: Three meals and name matching do not establish quantities, freshness, allergy safety or household cost savings.
audit.Hiring value: Explaining derived state and designing recovery around an editable source of truth.
audit.Main weakness: Weakest general opener: familiar category, very small data model and no household validation. Repair it through bounded utility rather than more screens.
